new_statements.quote: En ti, il n'existe pas de signes démarcatifs comme c'est le cas avec d'autres langues (l'accent par exemple en anglais...) - Cependant, l'analyse des combinaisons revèle un certain nombre de signes démarcatifs fondés sur les incompatibilités. - L'occlusion glottale ʔ marque toujours la finale de mot. - La présence d'un groupe de consonnes (C + c, N + C) signale toujours un début de mot. [...] La fonction démarcative n'étant que secondaire, nous ne nous attardons pas dessus. [p. 22:] Le ti est une langue à tons, c'est-à-dire qu'elle utilise les différences de hauteur de la voix lors de l'exécution des mots pour distinguer des significations.
new_statements.translation: In Ti there are no demarcative signs as there are in other languages (accent, for instance, in English...). However, analysis of the combinations reveals a certain number of demarcative signs based on incompatibilities. The glottal stop ʔ always marks the end of a word. The presence of a consonant cluster (C + c, N + C) always signals the beginning of a word. [...] Since the demarcative function is only secondary, we do not dwell on it. [p. 22:] Ti is a tone language, that is, it uses differences in voice pitch in the production of words to distinguish meanings.
new_statements.citation: Nusi, Jean. 1986. Esquisse phonologique du ti, parler des ti de la province de l'Ouest-Cameroun. Mémoire de Maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé. 137 pp.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is a two-level tone language (H, L tonemes, plus rising and falling contours); the author states explicitly that there is no demarcative accent of the English type — word boundaries are signalled only segmentally (final glottal stop, initial clusters). No positional word-stress rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author notes only that contour tones are rare in the lexicon but frequent in grammatical constructions (p. 23).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (mot phonologique); statement made in the chapter on phoneme combinations within the phonological word. Data from the Bati chiefdom at Galim (Bamboutos) with informants in Yaoundé.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: The only opened source, Nusi 1986, does NOT describe bati1251. Its 'ti' is the language of the Bati chiefdom at Galim (Bamboutos, West Province): the author classifies it as Eastern Grassfields (Mbam-Nkam), 85.8% similar to Mungaka [mhk] (pp. 6-14), and Glottolog itself files a duplicate record of the same thesis ('Nusi 2000', ref id 157518, hdl 11858/00-001M-0000-0012-803B-D) under mung1266. The target bati1251 = Mbam-group Bati [btc] of Kelleng/Nyambat/Mbougué (Nyanon, Littoral / Mbam-et-Inoubou, Centre; alt. Bati Ba Ngong, Bati de Brousse); Makon 2020 (Glottolog language code 'Bati of Kelleng') and Mbogol 2005 are the descriptions of that language. If the Nusi statement is used at all it belongs under mung1266 (Mungaka) or an unlisted Nun-group variety 'Ti / Bati of Galim', not bati1251.

sources.note: Deposit page lists 155 items (audio/video/ELAN wordlist elicitation, grammar elicitation, interviews from Kelleng, Nyambat, Mbougué, Mbay-Bati; a 'Cross-dialectal-Description' session comparing Basaa (Mbene) with Nyambat and Kelleng Bati). No written phonology/grammar item visible; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Used for identity: bati1251 = Mbam-group Bati [btc], alt. names Bati Ba Ngong / Bati de Brousse, Littoral (Nyanon) and Centre (Mbam-et-Inoubou), 800 speakers (1975); subclassification refs Boone et al. 1999, Boyd 2015, Grant 1992. Glottolog also files Nusi's thesis a second time as 'Nusi 2000' (id 157518) under mung1266 (Mungaka).
